title: Consolidate routing adapters and deprecate legacy fallback implementations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The smart routing layer currently contains multiple parallel adapter implementations and several legacy fallback paths introduced over time. This has caused inconsistent behavior across regions, duplicated metric instrumentation, and multiple contention points in the hot path. We've seen incidents where fallback reconciliation took >2s at p99 because of lock contention and redundant region probes.

Goal: Reduce cognitive and runtime complexity of the routing hot path by consolidating adapter interfaces, removing deprecated fallback shims, and introducing a single, testable fallback graph with explicit invariants. Outcomes we want: consistent failure semantics across regions, measurable reduction in p99 route-selection latency, simpler instrumentation, and a migration strategy that maintains availability during rollout.

Scope:
- Extract a minimal PolicyAdapter interface used by the SmartRouter hotpath.
- Implement a single FallbackCoordinator that replaces three legacy fallback implementations and the region-specific heuristics.
- Replace per-region probe code with a pluggable RegionHealth interface and centralize decisions.
- Remove global locks by converting key-critical state to lock-free structures (atomic pointers / sharded maps) where safe.
- Add comprehensive unit + integration tests and introduce synthetic perf benchmarks for common traffic shapes.

Out of scope: full rewrite of SmartRouter control plane or changes to routing policy DSL. This ticket focuses on the runtime refactor and migration for stable behavior and performance improvements.
tasks: Design PolicyAdapter minimal surface and publish spec (API + thread-safety notes)
Implement FallbackCoordinator with deterministic graph evaluation and unit tests
Create RegionHealth interface and migrate regional probes into adapters
Replace three legacy fallback modules: legacy_fallback_a, legacy_fallback_b, regional_heuristics
Add canary flag and feature-flag gating for coordinator per-cluster
Write integration tests that exercise multi-region failover and fallback chaining
Add perf harness and run baseline vs refactor for p50/p95/p99 selection latency
Docs: update internal design doc and add runbook for rollback scenarios
acceptance_criteria: All existing unit and integration tests for SmartRouter pass against refactor branch
p99 route-selection latency reduced by >= 20% on synthetic production-like workload
Fallback reconciliation success rate >= 99.9% under normal load and graceful under degraded node counts
No customer-facing error-rate increase during a staged canary rollout (observability verification)
All legacy fallback modules removed from mainline and deprecated code gated behind feature flag until final cutover
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag; 2) Canary on a single low-traffic region for 24h with traffic shadowing; 3) Enable coordinator for 10% of clusters with automated rollback on regression; 4) Gradually expand to 50% then 100% over 4 days while monitoring metrics and oncall feedback; 5) Remove legacy code and cleanup flags in subsequent release.
migration_steps:
- Ensure PolicyAdapter shim exists that routes calls to old adapters.
- Deploy refactor behind feature flag and shadow real traffic to exercise new fallback graph.
- Validate metrics and integration tests in canary.
- Flip feature flag for incremental clusters.
- After 72h stable at 100% enable, schedule a small change window to remove legacy modules and run a full CI pipeline.
benchmarks_goal: Baseline p99 selection latency: 73ms. Target after refactor: <=58ms (>=20% improvement). Also target 10-15% reduction in CPU usage on routing hotpath for typical batching traffic.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: subtle semantic differences in fallback ordering could surface as client-facing failures. Mitigation: produce a compatibility test suite that replays historical routing decisions and assert identical outcomes for the same inputs (when feature flag off). Risk: migration could cause transient increases in tail latency. Mitigation: conservative canary with automatic rollback and circuit-breakers in coordinator.
